title: Still God, experiencing life within the rules
identity: In Uday’s teaching, entering this game does not mean that we cease to be God. We are the same Creator who voluntarily entered different lives without the unrestricted powers of the Creator available to each individual role. The limitation belongs to the way the game is experienced; it does not remove our shared divine identity.
example: Why enter without those powers? Uday explains that, with every power freely available, there would be no need for a body or a car: nothing would need to be reached, learned or experienced through them. To have the experiences of embodied life, the Creator voluntarily enters a game with different rules, needs and limitations. Living through these conditions is the purpose of entry in this account.
recognition: Remembering “I am the Creator” therefore means recognizing who is having the experience while continuing to live within the game’s rules. Recognizing this identity does not give the individual unrestricted powers or the ability to rewrite the design from inside. The same divine identity belongs to everyone, not only to the person who understands the teaching.
meditationTitle: Explore identity and the purpose of experience in meditation
meditation: Uday invites us to examine this explanation through meditation and reflection: if every power were available without limitation, what role would a body, a journey or a relationship play? What does it mean for the same Creator to experience life through a limited role? Meditation is a setting for exploring and understanding this spiritual account, rather than a requirement to acquire powers or a proof that the account is fact.
question: Does entering the game mean that we are no longer God?
